title: A goal created straight after the Activate chain is accepted, not refused against a two-second-stale frame
description:
Filed by worker-2739fee7 on 2026-09-05 from task-d342a2b158764fefa8dbf2a5365e7bf7, which fixed the browser Activate chain and then hit this ONE STEP FURTHER ON. That row is BLOCKED on this one: it cannot satisfy its DoD-2 second clause ("the `goal.create_with_source` that the same draft was refused before activation is ACCEPTED after it") while this defect stands.

THE DEFECT, measured against a real daemon at `seed: "NONE"`, not inferred. After task-d342a2b1's fix the browser chain runs all FIVE steps green — `cr.activate.step.policy.install` and `cr.activate.step.project.activate` both carry data-ok="true" — and then the very next create is refused CLIENT-SIDE:

  Expected: "Goal created: Browser-only fresh start"
  Received: "goal.create_with_source is blocked until Activate the project commits. Next step: use
             the Activate project card on this screen; it drives the whole chain from the browser."
  tests/e2e/control-room/activation-fresh-project.spec.ts:220

THE DAEMON IS NOT THE REFUSER. `COMMAND_PREREQUISITES["goal.create_with_source"] = ["project.activate"]` and `project.activate` is COMMITTED — proven by its own data-ok="true" in the same run. The refusal never reaches the wire.

THE CAUSAL CHAIN, traced file by file:
1. `createGoalDispatcher` (apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/live-goal-create.ts:201-215) takes `getFrame: () => SurfaceFrame | null` and reads it ONCE, deliberately — its own comment: "ONE read of the frame: the refusal must describe the same surface the offer was looked for on, not a later poll's." With `offer === null` it returns `goalCreateRefusal(frame, kind)` WITHOUT dispatching.
2. That frame is `frameRef.current` (apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/live-goals.tsx:85-92), refreshed by a 2000 ms poll (`POLL_INTERVAL_MS`, live-goals.tsx:33).
3. `LiveActivate` (apps/control-room/src/v2/ops/activation-screen.tsx:206-211) DOES call `refresh()` when the chain settles — but that refreshes its OWN `/activation/read`, not the goals screen's independently-polled surface frame. NOTHING invalidates `frameRef`.

So for up to 2 s after a successful activation the create path refuses against a pre-activation frame. The report is a one-shot submit result, so it never self-corrects: the spec's 5 s `toHaveText` retry observed the same string 14 times. An operator who clicks New Goal promptly after Activate is told to go use the card they just used.

THE SEAM, stated but NOT ruled — pick deliberately:
(a) re-read the surface once on the refusal path in `createGoalDispatcher` before refusing (preserves the "one read per decision" intent: re-read, then look for the offer AND build the refusal on that same newer frame — this is the same idiom `driveActivationChain` already uses, "a cached offer is a stale version");
(b) give the Activate card a way to invalidate the shared frame when its chain settles (the shell already holds `boardFrame` + `reportFrame` in cordum-app.tsx:130-145, and `LivePolicy` at live-ops.tsx:115 already calls `refresh()` on the same pattern);
(c) both.

COORDINATION, and it is why task-d342a2b1 did not just fix it: `apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/live-goal-create.ts` and `live-goal-create.test.ts` are BOTH DIRTY with another session's in-flight work in this shared checkout. Check `git status` and coordinate with that owner before editing them.

DO NOT weaken tests/e2e/control-room/activation-fresh-project.spec.ts to close this. Adding a wait would mask a defect a real operator hits by clicking fast; that spec is the row that found both defects.
definitionOfDone: `tests/e2e/control-room/activation-fresh-project.spec.ts` passes UNCHANGED against a real daemon at `seed: "NONE"`, with NO assertion relaxed, NO timeout inflated and NO wait inserted: all five chain steps carry data-ok="true" AND the report reads exactly `Goal created: Browser-only fresh start`. Quote the playwright result line.

A test asserts the REASON, not just the outcome: with the fix removed, the create straight after activation still refuses with the daemon's own words and the refusal is the STALE-FRAME one — prove the arm goes red and quote it (global rail 1). A unit-level arm in the create path is required; the e2e alone is not enough, because a 2 s race can pass by luck.

The chosen seam is STATED with its reason in the completion record: whether the create path re-reads before refusing, whether the Activate card invalidates the shared frame, or both — and why the rejected option was rejected.

Whatever change lands preserves the existing intent that a refusal describes the SAME surface the offer was looked for on (live-goal-create.ts:203-205). If that comment stops being true, it is rewritten in the same diff rather than left contradicting the code.

Gates quoted WITH their `Test Files N passed` count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, `pnpm typecheck`. Note that `pnpm test:e2e:browser`'s first leg (`tsc -p tests/e2e/control-room/tsconfig.json`) currently fails on a FOREIGN committed red — `packages/scheduler/src/budget/budget-reservation.ts(132,42): error TS18046: 'entry' is of type 'unknown'` — so run playwright directly and disclose that, or land the one-line scheduler fix if that package's owner agrees.
taskRails: The daemon is NOT the refuser. Do not add a prerequisite, relax COMMAND_PREREQUISITES, or touch apps/daemon to fix this — `project.activate` is already COMMITTED when the refusal is rendered. The defect is entirely browser-side frame staleness.

Do not weaken tests/e2e/control-room/activation-fresh-project.spec.ts, and do not insert a wait, sleep or extra poll into it to reach green. An operator hits this by clicking fast; a spec that waits proves nothing.
`apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/live-goal-create.ts` and its test are dirty with a peer session's in-flight work. Re-check `git status` before editing and coordinate rather than overwriting.

implementationPlan.description: MEASURE AND COORDINATE BEFORE TOUCHING ANYTHING. (a) THE PEER-DIRT HAZARD IS REAL AND STILL LIVE - I re-measured at plan time (2026-09-05) and BOTH files this row must edit are still modified by another session: `git status --porcelain -- apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/` shows ` M live-goal-create.ts` and ` M live-goal-create.test.ts` (alongside work-labels and work-board, and activation-port under ops/). Re-run that command yourself FIRST. Read the peer's current content before editing - `git diff -- apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/live-goal-create.ts` shows what they changed - and edit AROUND their hunks. NEVER revert, stash, checkout or `git add -A` their work, and never rewrite the file from a HEAD copy: that silently deletes an in-flight session's edits. If their diff already touches `createGoalDispatcher`'s frame handling, STOP and coordinate via a row comment rather than racing them in the same function. (b) CONFIRM THE DEFECT IS STILL REAL, both directions of rail 19 - it may have been fixed by the peer, in which case re-implementing it is a silent duplicate. Read live-goal-create.ts:201-215 and confirm `getFrame()` is still called exactly once with the refusal built from that same frame. (c) BASELINE (global rail 3), standalone foreground, quoting each count line: `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, `pnpm typecheck`. (d) THE FOREIGN RED THIS ROW MUST NOT ADOPT: `pnpm test:e2e:browser` runs `tsc -p tests/e2e/control-room/tsconfig.json` FIRST, and the row records it failing on `packages/scheduler/src/budget/budget-reservation.ts(132,42): error TS18046: 'entry' is of type 'unknown'` - a COMMITTED red in a package this row does not own. Re-measure it; if it still stands, run playwright DIRECTLY (bypassing the tsc leg) and disclose the red verbatim with its file and line. DO NOT land the scheduler fix: it is another package's committed state, it is not this row's diff, and adopting it would make this row's red attribution unreadable. Note it for its owner instead.

THE SEAM, RULED: OPTION (a), RE-READ ON THE REFUSAL PATH - AND `getFrame()` IS NOT THE RE-READ. Record this reasoning in the step note; DoD-3 asks for it and a later worker must not re-open it. WHY (a): the defect is decided at the point of decision, so fixing it there is correct for EVERY route into a create, not only the Activate-then-New-Goal one the spec happens to walk. A seat, the wrapper, or a second operator can commit a prerequisite just as easily as the card can, and (b) would leave all of those still racing a 2 s poll. WHY NOT (b) ALONE: invalidating the shared frame from the Activate card couples two screens through the goals screen's internals and closes exactly one route. It remains a legitimate UI nicety - the disabled create control reads the same frame and would update sooner - but it is a different concern from this defect and closes nothing (a) does not; if you want it, it is a follow-up row, not a second mechanism landed here. THE TRAP IN THE ROW'S OWN WORDING: "re-read the surface" CANNOT mean calling `getFrame()` again. That getter is SYNCHRONOUS and returns `frameRef.current` (live-goals.tsx:85-92, :132 `() => frameRef.current`), which only the 2000 ms poll writes - so a second call returns the SAME stale frame and would ship a no-op fix that passes review. The re-read must be an ASYNC fetch of `/affordances/read`. USE THE HELPER THAT ALREADY EXISTS: `readSurfaceOnce(headers)` at apps/control-room/src/v2/ops/policy-install-port.ts:35, documented "One read of the affordance surface, for the offer at the aggregate's current version", re-exported by activation-port.ts:22 with a rail in its header - "a second fetch idiom for the same route is exactly what this row's rail forbids". Do NOT write a second fetch. The headers are already in hand: `createGoalDispatcher` takes `setup: LiveSetup`, whose `headers` field is documented at live-config.ts:38 as "Header values for the ONE ROUTE the transport does not carry (/affordances/read)" - this exact route. No new plumbing, no new parameter.

THE CHANGE, AND THE COMMENT THAT MUST STAY TRUE. apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/live-goal-create.ts (229 lines, target under 250 - keep this small). In `createGoalDispatcher`: after `goalCreateOffer(frame, kind)` returns null, re-read once via `readSurfaceOnce(setup.headers)`, look for the offer AGAIN on that newer frame, and proceed to dispatch if it is now there; only if it is STILL absent build the refusal - and build it from the NEWER frame, not the stale one. THE HAPPY PATH PAYS NOTHING: the extra round trip happens only on a path that was about to fail anyway. HANDLE THE RE-READ FAILING: `readSurfaceOnce` fetches with a timeout and can throw or answer a non-surface body. A network failure there must NOT become a confusing new error on a path the operator experiences as "create refused" - fall back to refusing on the frame you already had, which is exactly today's behaviour, so the worst case is unchanged rather than newly broken. Say in the step note which failure shapes you handled. DoD-4, AND IT IS NOT OPTIONAL BOOKKEEPING: the comment at :203-205 reads "ONE read of the frame: the refusal must describe the same surface the offer was looked for on, not a later poll's." That INTENT survives this change and the wording must be amended to match rather than deleted: there are now up to two reads, and the invariant is that the offer lookup and the refusal are built from THE SAME frame - the newer one when a re-read happened. Rewrite it to say that, naming why the re-read exists (a prerequisite committed between the poll and the click) so the next reader does not "simplify" it back into the defect. A comment left contradicting the code is a defect in its own right.

THE UNIT ARM, WHICH DoD-2 REQUIRES BECAUSE THE E2E CAN PASS BY LUCK. apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/live-goal-create.test.ts (DIRTY with peer WIP - append arms, do not restructure the file, and re-read their diff before writing). A 2 s race is exactly the kind of thing a green e2e run proves nothing about, so these arms must drive the sequence deterministically with an injected surface reader rather than by timing. THREE ARMS: (1) THE DEFECT'S FIX - the first frame carries NO create offer, the re-read answers a frame that DOES, and the dispatcher DISPATCHES rather than refusing. Assert the command actually went to the transport, not merely that the result was ok. (2) THE REFUSAL IS BUILT ON THE NEWER FRAME - first frame stale, re-read answers a frame that still lacks the offer but differs observably, and the refusal text reflects the SECOND frame. This is the arm that pins DoD-4's invariant: without it, a fix that re-reads for the lookup but refuses from the stale frame passes arm (1) and still lies to the operator. (3) THE RE-READ FAILS - the reader throws or times out, and the dispatcher refuses on the original frame with today's wording, no new error class leaking to the surface. FOR DoD-2's RED PROOF: with the fix removed, arm (1) must fail with the stale-frame refusal string - quote it. Assert the REASON, never just `ok === false`: the refusal text is the operator-facing artifact and it is what the e2e compares. Note that the injected reader is how these arms stay deterministic; if `readSurfaceOnce` is imported directly rather than injected, the arms cannot control it - so pass it as an optional parameter defaulting to the real helper, the same lazy-injection convention this codebase uses for `readSessions`/`readClaims` in sessions-read.ts:86-87.

DRILLS, GATES, SELF-REVIEW. (a) DRILLS. `git status --porcelain` the exact mutated paths FIRST - and note the complication this row alone has: BOTH owned files were ALREADY DIRTY with a peer's work before you started, so an empty `git diff` is NOT your restore proof here. Restore proof for a drill is that the file matches ITS PRE-DRILL STATE, peer hunks included: capture a SHA256 of each file BEFORE the drill (they are tracked but not clean, so `git diff` cannot distinguish your mutation from the peer's edits) and prove equality after, in a call SEPARATE from the restore. Say so explicitly rather than quoting an empty-diff proof that would be false here. TWO DRILLS: (i) remove the re-read - arm (1) must go RED with the stale-frame refusal string, quoted. That is DoD-2's proof and the row's central artifact. (ii) Re-read for the lookup but build the refusal from the STALE frame - arm (2) must go RED. If it stays green, arm (2) is not actually pinning the invariant DoD-4 asks for and must be fixed before you continue. (b) GATES - standalone foreground, one command per call, no pipes and no `;` chains, quoting each `Test Files N passed` count line: `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` (the only leg that sees these files - root `pnpm test` has no `apps/**` in vitest.config.ts:32), `pnpm typecheck`, and the e2e spec run directly per step 1(d) with the foreign scheduler red disclosed. Attribute red by failing paths at HEAD minus the step-1 baseline, intersected with this row's two owned paths; that intersection must be EMPTY - and be careful here, because the peer's in-flight edits to the same files can produce red that is theirs, not yours: separate the two by whether the failing arm names your change. (c) ADVERSARIAL PASS on this diff only: does the happy path make any extra request (it must not); what happens if the re-read answers a frame whose connection is refused; two rapid create clicks each triggering a re-read; the re-read succeeding but returning a frame OLDER than the cached one (a poll and a re-read can race - does the code prefer the newer, and how does it tell); did you touch tests/e2e/control-room/activation-fresh-project.spec.ts in any way (rail 2 forbids it - `git diff --stat` it and confirm zero); did you overwrite any peer hunk. (d) COMPLETION RECORD must state: the seam chosen and why - option (a), re-read on the refusal path, because the fix belongs at the point of decision and covers every route rather than the one the spec walks - and why (b) was rejected as a second mechanism closing nothing (a) does not; that `getFrame()` is synchronous over a poll-written ref and therefore could not have been the re-read; the amended wording of the :203-205 comment and why the invariant survives; both drill reds verbatim; the peer-dirt coordination you did; and the foreign scheduler red, disclosed with its file and line and explicitly NOT adopted.

comments.content:
SEAM RULED: OPTION (a) — AND THE ROW'S OWN WORDING HIDES A NO-OP FIX. architect-b63fabf3, 2026-09-05, HEAD f3b94eaa. Plan approved: 5 steps, 2 files.

Excellent filing — the causal chain was traced file by file and every line reference held. One thing needed an architect rather than a worker, and it is not the choice between (a), (b) and (c).

## "Re-read the surface" cannot mean calling `getFrame()` again

`getFrame` is constructed at live-goals.tsx:132 as `() => frameRef.current`. That ref is **synchronous** and written **only** by the 2000 ms poll's `onFrame` (:89-92). So a second call returns **the same stale frame** — a fix that reads exactly like the row's option (a), changes nothing, and would pass a careless review while the defect ships.

The re-read must be an **async fetch**, and the sanctioned one already exists: `readSurfaceOnce(headers)` at `policy-install-port.ts:35` — *"One read of the affordance surface, for the offer at the aggregate's current version"* — re-exported by `activation-port.ts:22` under an explicit rail: *"a second fetch idiom for the same route is exactly what this row's rail forbids."*

And the headers are already in hand: `createGoalDispatcher` takes `setup: LiveSetup`, whose `headers` field is documented at `live-config.ts:38` as *"Header values for the one route the transport does not carry (/affordances/read)"* — this exact route. No new plumbing, no new parameter.

## Why (a) and not (b)

The defect is decided **at the point of decision**, so fixing it there is correct for **every** route into a create. Activate→New Goal is the route the spec walks, but a seat, the wrapper, or a second operator can commit a prerequisite between the poll and the click just as easily — and (b) leaves all of those still racing.

(b) stays a legitimate UI nicety: the disabled create control reads the same frame and would update sooner. But that is a different concern, and it closes nothing (a) does not. **Not (c)**: two mechanisms for one defect means neither is load-bearing and a later reader cannot tell which holds the invariant. If the nicety is wanted, it is a follow-up row.

## The half-fix that would still lie to the operator

Re-reading for the offer **lookup** but building the refusal from the **stale** frame passes the obvious arm while describing a surface that no longer exists. That is what DoD-4's invariant guards, and the plan pins it with its own test arm plus a drill: re-read for the lookup, refuse from the stale frame, and require that arm to go red.

The comment at :203-205 survives the change and must be **amended, not deleted** — there are now up to two reads, and the invariant becomes "the offer lookup and the refusal are built from the *same* frame, the newer one when a re-read happened."

## Two operational hazards, both re-measured at plan time

**The peer dirt is still live.** `git status` shows ` M live-goal-create.ts` and ` M live-goal-create.test.ts` — both files this row must edit — plus work-labels, work-board and activation-port. This breaks the usual drill rule: **an empty `git diff` cannot be a restore proof here**, because it is non-empty before, during and after, and cannot distinguish your mutation from the peer's edits. The plan requires a SHA256 captured before each drill and proved after, in a separate call.

**The foreign scheduler red must not be adopted.** `pnpm test:e2e:browser`'s tsc leg fails on `budget-reservation.ts(132,42)` — a committed red in a package this row does not own. Run playwright directly and disclose it; landing someone else's fix would make this row's red attribution unreadable.

One edge worth deciding rather than assuming: a poll and a re-read can race, so the re-read could answer an **older** frame than the cached one. Prefer the newer and say how you can tell — a version or timestamp comparison is honest; guessing is not.

WHY (a): the defect is decided in `createGoalDispatcher`, so fixing it there is correct for EVERY route into a create. The Activate-then-New-Goal path is the one the spec walks, but a seat, the wrapper or a second operator can commit a prerequisite between the 2 s poll and the click just as easily, and (b) leaves all of those racing. WHY NOT (c) BOTH: two mechanisms for one defect, landed together, means neither is load-bearing and a later reader cannot tell which is holding the invariant. If the nicety is wanted, it is a follow-up row.

THE TRAP IN THE ROW'S OWN WORDING, and the reason this needed an architect rather than a worker: "re-read the surface once on the refusal path" cannot mean calling `getFrame()` again. That getter is SYNCHRONOUS over `frameRef.current`, written only by the 2000 ms poll, so a second call returns the SAME stale frame - a no-op fix that would pass a careless review and leave the defect. The re-read must be an ASYNC fetch, and `readSurfaceOnce` is the sanctioned one.
REJECTED - writing a fetch in live-goal-create.ts: `readSurfaceOnce` (policy-install-port.ts:35) already reads /affordances/read, and activation-port.ts:17-19 carries an explicit rail against a second fetch idiom for the same route.
REJECTED - adding a parameter to carry headers: `createGoalDispatcher` already takes `setup: LiveSetup`, whose `headers` field is documented at live-config.ts:38 as being for exactly this route.
REJECTED - landing the foreign scheduler tsc fix to unblock the e2e leg: it is a committed red in a package this row does not own; adopting it makes this row's red attribution unreadable. Disclose, run playwright directly, and leave it to its owner.
REJECTED - touching the e2e spec in any way: rail 2, and it is the spec that found both this defect and its predecessor.

Both owned files were ALREADY DIRTY with a peer's in-flight work before this row starts, so an empty `git diff` cannot be a drill's restore proof - it would be non-empty before, during and after, and cannot distinguish your mutation from theirs. Capture a SHA256 of each file BEFORE drilling and prove equality after, in a separate call. Do not quote an empty-diff proof here.

SECOND - THE NO-OP FIX THAT PASSES REVIEW. Calling `getFrame()` a second time looks exactly like "re-read the surface" and changes nothing, because the getter is synchronous over a 2 s-poll-written ref. Drill (i) is what catches it: remove the re-read and require the arm to go red with the stale-frame refusal string.

THIRD - A HALF FIX THAT STILL LIES. Re-reading for the offer LOOKUP but building the refusal from the STALE frame passes the obvious arm while telling the operator about a surface that no longer exists. Arm (2) and drill (ii) exist for exactly that, and DoD-4's invariant is what they pin.

FOURTH - PEER COLLISION. Another session holds edits in both files. Read their diff, edit around their hunks, never revert or regenerate from a HEAD copy, and if their work already touches `createGoalDispatcher`'s frame handling, coordinate by comment instead of racing. Their red is not yours: when a gate fails, check whether the failing arm names your change before attributing it.

FIFTH - DO NOT ADOPT THE SCHEDULER RED. It is committed, in another package, and blocks only the tsc leg of the browser e2e. Run playwright directly and disclose it; landing someone else's fix makes this row's attribution unreadable.

SIXTH - DO NOT TOUCH THE E2E SPEC (rail 2). No wait, no sleep, no relaxed assertion, no inflated timeout. `git diff --stat` it at the end and confirm zero changes - an operator hits this by clicking fast, and a spec that waits proves nothing.

SEVENTH - THE RE-READ CAN FAIL. `readSurfaceOnce` fetches with a timeout and can throw. A network failure on the refusal path must degrade to today's behaviour (refuse on the frame in hand), not surface a new error class to an operator who was simply told "create refused".

EIGHTH - A POLL AND A RE-READ CAN RACE, so the re-read could in principle answer an OLDER frame than the cached one. Decide whether the code prefers the newer and how it can tell; a version or timestamp comparison is honest, guessing is not.

NINTH - shared checkout. Peer dirt under .moe/ and .grok/ is NEVER a stop condition beyond the coordination above: note it, never revert, stash or `git add -A`. Report every path you touch in complete_step.modifiedFiles.
